newsitem.title: USA: Cavallo says Argentina needs to deepen reforms.
newsitem.headline: Cavallo says Argentina needs to deepen reforms.

text.p: Argentina has made tremendous progress in implementing economic reforms and reducing inflation, but the country still needs to deepen its labor reforms to fight the current high rate of unemployment, said Domingo Cavallo, Argentina's former economy minister.

Speaking at a meeting sponsored by the Americas Society here, Cavallo said: "I am very optimistic about growth and stability for my country. Although it doesn't mean we don't have problems. Unemployment is still a problem."
According to the latest government figures released at the end of 1996 for the month October, Argentina's unemployment rate was 17.3 percent.

"To cope with high unemployment and to provide solutions for poverty...we have to deepen the reforms and extend out reforms. In terms of creating new jobs, it is important to deepen the reforms of the labor legisation," Cavallo said.
However, Cavallo said Argentina's Congress was not devoting enough time to the discussion of labor legislation.
"Unfortunately, our Congration and the executive (branch) can only use its power, which is limited by the constitution, to introduce some reforms," he said.
In addition to labor reform, Cavallo said there was "huge potential demand" for job creation in housing construction and urban infrastructure in Argentina.
